candidates.title: The Pocket Migration Before Leaving
suggested_slide_arc: Entryway: Zuv is ready to leave, keys in hand, while Aachu arrives with a tiny serious collection of lip balm, hair tie, tissue, and one mysterious small object.
Aachu silently loads his jacket pockets like she is packing a very handsome emergency kit.
Zuv discovers he is now carrying half her world and gives her the look; she adds one more thing anyway.
Payoff: outside the door, she reaches for something and he produces it instantly, absurdly proud.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: Zuv stands by the door in a clean three-quarter pose, one hand holding keys, while Aachu stands beside him placing a hair tie into his jacket pocket with complete seriousness.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: Aachu holds out her hand without looking; Zuv places the exact tiny item into her palm like a trained magician, both faces readable and warm.
candidates.visual_potential: Strong single-location doorway staging, clear hands, tactile props, clean upper-middle negative space for text, and a recurring pocket gag that can escalate without crowding the frame.
failure_risks: Tiny props could become unreadable if over-specified.
Too many pocket items could clutter the lower frame.
Needs restraint so it does not become a generic leaving-the-house checklist.

candidates.title: The Wet-Nails Assistant Shift
suggested_slide_arc: Aachu sits at the table with freshly painted nails held up like fragile evidence; Zuv clocks that both her hands are now unavailable.
He opens snacks, turns a page, and holds a glass with exaggerated care while she stays perfectly still.
The helper job expands until he is holding too many harmless little things, still trying to look composed.
Payoff: Zuv has one accidental painted pinky nail and is still proudly feeding her a bite.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: Aachu sits upright at a small table, fingers spread to dry, nail polish bottle visible; Zuv leans in from the side holding an opened snack packet like he has accepted a sacred duty.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: Zuv presents his accidentally painted pinky with mock dignity while Aachu laughs, her hands still hovering safely above the table.
candidates.visual_potential: Very stageable, intimate, funny, and object-led. The hands carry the joke, but faces stay separated and readable. Tabletop gives excellent negative space for handwritten text.
failure_risks: Hands and fingers need simplified natural anatomy.
Nail details should not become tiny beauty-product clutter.
Avoid servant/queen staging that feels mean instead of tender.

candidates.title: The Fridge Tetris Treaty
suggested_slide_arc: Kitchen: the fridge is open, containers are lined on the counter, and both of them are pretending this is not a serious engineering problem.
Aachu rotates one container into the only correct position while Zuv confidently offers the wrong round bowl.
They pause over one impossible gap, hands hovering, faces readable from the side.
Payoff: the fridge is perfectly arranged, with one dessert box placed in the easiest front spot for Aachu.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: Open fridge on one side, counter on the other, Aachu holding a square container and Zuv holding a round bowl, both looking at the shelf like it personally betrayed them.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: Zuv presents the finished fridge arrangement with quiet pride; Aachu notices her favorite little dessert box placed front and center.
candidates.visual_potential: Fresh domestic puzzle with strong prop geometry, clean kitchen staging, and a payoff that proves care without needing explanatory microtext.
failure_risks: Open fridge shelves can become visually busy.
Container shapes must stay readable without labels.
Lighting from the fridge should not push the style toward digital glow.

top_pick.title: The Pocket Migration Before Leaving
top_pick.reason: It has the cleanest frame language: doorway, hands, pockets, tiny props, readable faces, and a payoff that is immediately visual. It can be funny without becoming loud, and warm without needing a quote-card rescue.

visual_risks: Keep small props symbolic and low-count: hair tie, lip balm, tissue, keys, one extra object maximum per slide.
Do not place faces too close together in doorway compositions.
Reserve upper-middle negative space for exact baked-in handwritten text.
Avoid pocket labels, phone screens, receipts, or any microtext-dependent joke.
Keep every idea to one main location unless Story Room proves a second location is necessary.

slide_count_hints.The Pocket Migration Before Leaving: 4 slides is ideal; 3 would rush the escalation, 5 would over-explain the pocket gag.
slide_count_hints.The Wet-Nails Assistant Shift: 4 slides; the helper escalation needs one middle beat before the painted-pinky payoff.
slide_count_hints.The Fridge Tetris Treaty: 3 or 4 slides; choose 3 if the visual puzzle is strong, 4 only if the dessert payoff needs setup.
